title: Navimower 0.4.5

## Stable release

Navimower 0.4.5 is primarily a **state ownership, reliability and backend architecture** release.

The goal of this release cycle was to make the integration the authoritative owner of mower/task semantics, retained mowing state and expensive map preparation, while giving frontends a cleaner and more stable contract.

## Highlights

### Persistent current-cycle mowing state

Navimower now keeps a persistent per-zone current-cycle model.

- ZoneLedger owns the current/reset cycle identity for each zone.
- VendorTrailStore retains the vendor-provided mowing geometry for that zone/cycle.
- Retained trail survives pauses, charging, task changes, temporary cloud gaps and Home Assistant restarts.
- A zone trail is replaced only when there is evidence of a new/reset cycle for that same zone.
- MQTT movement is treated as the short live extension rather than replacing the retained vendor trail.

This greatly reduces cases where a valid current mowing trail disappeared or fell back to History simply because task/cloud state changed.

### Backend-prepared map resources

More rendering data is now prepared and cached by the integration:

- static/layout resources;
- current-cycle render artifacts;
- throttled Prepared Live route plus short live tail;
- content-addressed retained History resources;
- semantic live routes that distinguish cutting from travel/transit.

This reduces repeated JSON transfer and browser-side SVG reconstruction and provides a common source of truth for Single and Multi mower views.

### Backend map snapshots

Map snapshots are now Home Assistant image entities.

- normal/light snapshot enabled by default;
- optional dark snapshot, disabled by default;
- model-aware mower artwork;
- packaged Unicode font support for international zone names;
- independent caches, with disabled snapshot variants excluded from automatic rendering.

### Smarter Resume and ordered-run continuation

Navimower now owns Resume policy.

For an ordered multi-zone run, the integration can retain the original zone order, remove zones confirmed complete and continue only unfinished zones.

The higher-level navimower.continue_task action chooses between retained ordered-run continuation and vendor Resume.

Frontends can consume resume_available, resume_strategy, resume_reason and resume_evidence instead of guessing from mower activity.

### Target zone vs Planned zones

The public meanings are now explicit:

- **Target zone** = the immediate target;
- **Planned zones** = the full selected multi-zone task.

This makes automations safer, especially gate/navigation logic.

### Weather-aware task state

Vendor weather is now normalized into integration-owned task context.

Navimower distinguishes between:

- **Raining**
- **Rain delay** after rain has ended but the configured cooldown is still active.

Scheduler, pause reason and Resume logic use the same composed weather hold state.

Rain-delay deadlines survive reload/restart, and the last fresh rain state is persisted with an age bound so Home Assistant downtime during the rain-to-clear transition does not lose the cooldown edge.

### Capability discovery from evidence

Model-dependent features increasingly use positive capability/resource evidence instead of model-name assumptions.

LiDAR terrain capability is resource-driven: a valid vendor terrain package is authoritative, while model family is only a discovery/polling hint.

### Home Assistant Activity context

Meaningful mower and zone transitions can now carry a bounded integration-owned Home Assistant Context/cause event.

This improves Activity/Logbook attribution by providing more information about why a state changed.

### Privacy-safe public diagnostics

Home Assistant **Download diagnostics** is now an explicitly curated public-support report.

It retains useful technical evidence such as:

- state/activity/error codes;
- capabilities;
- source/freshness information;
- progress and counters;
- scheduler/Resume state;
- map/render/cache summaries;
- privacy-safe georeference/underlay diagnostics.

It intentionally excludes complete vendor raw payload bodies, raw notification/error bodies, user-authored labels/messages, exact mower-local geometry, full schedules/settings and complete georeference transform/control-point objects.

Development protocol capture remains separate from the stable support surface.

Normal MQTT startup INFO logs also mask both the configured mower serial and the official Smart Home device identifier.

## Compatibility

This release keeps compatibility fallbacks for the progressive prepared-render migration.

Navimower Map Card 0.3.7 is the matching frontend release for the new Resume, LiDAR capability, semantic trail and prepared-resource contracts.

Thanks to everyone who tested prereleases, supplied diagnostics and helped verify behavior across different mower families and firmware versions.
